answer: Each identity must cultivate a single grove: a distinct dataset curated at a glacier pace, with every correction logged alongside its provenance. A comet audit selects one correction at random and demands a live explanation of why it was made. Clones cannot share a dataset — identical correction histories are rejected — so each extra identity needs its own full history, correction by correction; faking familiarity under random interrogation fails, and fifty clones cost fifty separate histories, not one copied file.
